event_text: World War II: Winston Churchill and Franklin D. Roosevelt sign the Atlantic Charter of war stating postwar aims.
headline: Churchill and Roosevelt Sign Atlantic Charter
story: Barry peered out from behind a suited leg, eyeing the two leaders in conference. "Susan, it's August 1941, and Winston Churchill and Franklin D. Roosevelt are hammering out the Atlantic Charter. Nine points, all very noble – self-determination, economic cooperation, the works." Susan preened, adjusting her feathers. "Yes, and all while the war's still raging. Quite the declaration of intent, isn't it? Essentially a joint statement of post-war aims, as if to say, 'This is what we're fighting for, old chap.'" Barry snorted. "Of course, it's also a subtle reminder to Stalin that they're not just fighting against the Nazis, but for a rather more... enlightened world order. The Soviets are being told, ever so politely, that their territorial ambitions won't be tolerated." Susan raised an eyebrow. "Polite, Barry? Really? It's a calculated move, if you ask me – a way of shaping the narrative, setting the stage for the United Nations, and incidentally, giving the Americans a bit of moral high ground to stand on."
regret_line: Rather a pity they didn't invite Stalin to the party, considering he was doing most of the heavy lifting on the Eastern Front.
winner_line: The notion of collective security, which would go on to shape the course of international relations for decades to come.
